title: Risotto con Gorgonzola e Noci
subtitle: Gorgonzola and walnut risotto
excerpt: Risotto con gorgonzola e noci is a northern Italian winter risotto: creamy, pungent gorgonzola melted through Parmesan-finished rice, scattered with toasted walnuts. The richness of the cheese is balanced by the bitter crunch of the walnuts. It needs nothing else.
sourceNotes: Gorgonzola is produced in Lombardy and Piedmont under DOP protection. Using it to finish risotto is a classic Lombard technique. Walnuts are a natural pairing with blue cheese across northern Italian cooking.

content.text: Use gorgonzola dolce (the milder, creamier variety) if you want a subtler flavour; gorgonzola piccante gives a sharper, more pungent result. The gorgonzola replaces some of the butter in the final mantecatura, so the risotto does not become too rich. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes to deepen their flavour before adding them.

items.prepNote: the gorgonzola is salty -- taste before adding

content.text: Toast {{walnuts}} walnuts in a dry frying pan for 3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Cook {{onion}} onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed.
Add hot {{chicken-stock}} stock a ladleful at a time for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Remove from the heat.

Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter, {{parmesan}} Parmesan, and {{gorgonzola}} gorgonzola. Stir vigorously until the gorgonzola melts into the risotto. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve with the toasted walnuts scattered over.

items.cause: Gorgonzola is very salty and so is Parmesan.
items.fix: Do not add any salt until the gorgonzola and Parmesan are in. Taste and season only at the very end. Use unsalted stock if possible.

content.text: Gorgonzola is one of the great Italian blue cheeses, made in Lombardy under DOP status since 879 AD according to the consortium's records. Using it to finish risotto is a Lombard tradition found particularly around Milan and Novara. The walnut pairing follows Italian food logic -- the bitterness of the nut balances the sharpness of the cheese. It is a winter dish, served when the appetite wants something rich and filling.
